_README: Tenant -> 2020 census tract map for the FCC Broadband Data Collection (BDC)
Fixed Voice Subscription filing. Read by apps/api/scripts/bdc-voice-subscription-export.ts.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the BDC wants subscription counts by census tract, and the
tract comes from each customer's SERVICE ADDRESS. Those addresses live nowhere in
Connect (TenantBillingSettings.serviceAddress is NULL for every tenant; only 15 DIDs
are enrolled in VoIP.ms E911; the PBX has no address columns). On 2026-09-15 they were
assembled by hand from VoIP.ms e911Info plus Izzy's own answers, then geocoded to
tracts with the Census Bureau geocoder. Committing the result means the December round
and every round after it costs one command instead of an afternoon.
MAINTENANCE: when a tenant is added, moved, renamed or closed, update it here. The
export script REFUSES to emit a CSV if any tenant with extensions is missing from both
'tenants' and 'excluded' - a silent omission would under-report to the FCC.
⛔ Tracts are TEXT and must stay 11 digits (leading zeros matter). ⛔ Nothing in this
file touches VoIP.ms E911 registrations - Izzy, 2026-09-15: 'Don't turn on any e911
addresses now either. Just put the addresses in the report.'

serviceType.meaning: 1 = Interconnected VoIP subscriptions. Loopcom sells no VGE/TDM lines, so every row is service_type 1.

consumerPolicy.why: Every Loopcom customer is a business buying a business phone system; there are no residential/mass-market plans. So consumer_lines_or_subscriptions is 0 on every row and the whole book is Business/Govt.

stateLevelAllocation.why: Loopcom supplies no last-mile facilities - customers bring their own internet - so 100% of subscriptions are Over-the-Top and the 'All Other Subscriptions' block (End-User Type / Services Sold / Last-Mile Medium) is all zeros. ⛔ Never put Loopcom subscriptions in FTTP/Coaxial/FW-Satellite/Copper.
